_comment: WHAT A GNAWED GAP OPENS INTO. A cellar with the walls closer in: fewer rooms, tighter, the rooms closer together so a run between them is a squeeze rather than a walk. Browner and warmer than poured concrete, because this is bedding rather than building. Spacing is in TILES, so the cellar's distances inherited into a smaller box leave nowhere to seat the second hole a floor is guaranteed -- a tighter space needs them tighter. Its holes lean gnawed, which is what makes a warren feel like a NETWORK -- more of it runs sideways than down -- and max_rooms is how far it spreads at one depth before the space stops offering ways sideways.
